scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes the local R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` resource and the absence of a same-named R6 core StructureDefinition. Because no R6 counterpart was found, most element-level changes are assessed as consequences of resource removal rather than one-by-one path edits. Related R6 artifacts such as `Immunization`, `CarePlan`, `MedicationRequest`, `ServiceRequest`, `RequestOrchestration`, and `GuidanceResponse` were considered only to determine whether an obvious rename, split, or replacement existed; they were not fully assessed as their own artifacts.
outOfScope: Inherited/base-artifact changes from Element, BackboneElement, Resource, and DomainResource are excluded and should be assessed in the corresponding base-artifact reports.
R4 SearchParameter, CompartmentDefinition, CapabilityStatement, and OpenAPI consequences of removing ImmunizationRecommendation are related but separate artifact analyses.
The separate R4 ImmunizationEvaluation resource, which is also absent from the checked R6 package and is referenced by R4 ImmunizationRecommendation.supportingImmunization, is not assessed here.
External implementation-guide profiles, national immunization forecasting profiles, and jurisdiction-specific schedule rules are not assessed.
Full terminology expansion and clinical validity of vaccine forecasting codes are outside this local package-only review.

narrativeReportMd:
# ImmunizationRecommendation R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ImmunizationRecommendation` is present as a concrete R4 resource but is absent from the checked R6 ballot core package. This is a hard breaking change for any R4 instance, validator, parser, generated model, REST endpoint, or search workflow that uses `resourceType: "ImmunizationRecommendation"`.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 StructureDefinition, R4/R6 package indexes and metadata, R4 recommendation terminology artifacts, R6 FHIR type codes, and selected R6 immunization-related StructureDefinitions. Inherited `DomainResource`/base-element changes are intentionally excluded.

## Main migration themes
The primary issue is not a narrowed element or renamed child path; it is the apparent removal of the entire resource. R4 data containing patient-level vaccine forecasts, due/overdue/immune/contraindicated status, date criteria, supporting immunizations, and supporting patient information has no same-resource R6 target. R6 `Immunization` keeps some protocol-applied details for administered events and can point to plans/orders/recommendations via `basedOn`, but that does not preserve an independent point-in-time forecast resource.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the missing R6 artifact identity itself. A second high-impact finding is that the local forecasting content model, including mandatory `patient`, `date`, `recommendation`, and modifier `recommendation.forecastStatus`, disappears with the resource. Terminology artifacts specific to recommendation status/reason/date criteria are also not present in the checked R6 package.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to choose a migration pattern: profile an R6 workflow resource, define extensions, preserve R4 resources at a boundary, or use an implementation-guide-specific model. The local package evidence is strong for absence, but it does not explain the standards rationale or provide an official replacement mapping.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The removal appears avoidable from a wire-compatibility perspective: the base resource could have been retained as deprecated/trial-use while new workflow patterns were introduced. That would have preserved old instances and generated APIs, at the cost of carrying a resource the R6 ballot apparently no longer wants in core.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze the removed/related `ImmunizationEvaluation` artifact, R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation-*` search parameters, and candidate R6 workflow resources separately before selecting production migration rules.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ImmunizationRecommendation` appears to have been removed from R6 core, which is a hard R4→R6 break. The top migration concerns are loss of the `resourceType`, loss of the local forecasting content model including modifier `forecastStatus`, and lack of an official replacement/map. The main uncertainty is standards intent: the local package proves absence but not the recommended R6 migration pattern.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a discontinued resource unless an external IG or official cross-version map says otherwise. Migration will likely need a policy choice: keep R4 payloads at a boundary, map selected content into profiled R6 workflow resources plus extensions, or preserve complete forecast snapshots in a custom extension/contained artifact. A simple path rename is not available.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the resource is absent from the checked R6 ballot package because the assigned file is missing, package indexes and exact text searches found no `ImmunizationRecommendation`, and R6 type code systems list `Immunization` but not `ImmunizationRecommendation`. Confidence is lower for the best migration target because no official diff, narrative rationale, or ConceptMap was available locally.

findings.title: ImmunizationRecommendation resource is absent from the R6 ballot core package

oldState.summary: Concrete R4 resource with canonical StructureDefinition `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ImmunizationRecommendation`.

semanticText.short: Guidance or advice relating to an immunization
semanticText.definition: A patient's point-in-time set of recommendations (i.e. forecasting) according to a published schedule with optional supporting justification.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 defines a concrete, non-abstract resource whose wire identity is `resourceType: "ImmunizationRecommendation"`.

newState.summary: No R6 StructureDefinition, package-index entry, or fhir-type concept for ImmunizationRecommendation was found.
newState.narrativeMd: The assigned R6 file is absent and no same-named or obvious renamed resource was identified in the R6 core package.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new artifacts were matched by the assigned canonical/id/type. The R6 package has no exact file, no index entry, and no type-code concept for that identity. Related resources do not share the same point-in-time forecasting semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. A valid R4 JSON/XML instance with `resourceType: "ImmunizationRecommendation"` has no R6 core resource definition to validate against, and generated R6 model libraries are unlikely to contain a corresponding class, parser branch, REST type, or search endpoint.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource represents clinical vaccine forecasting recommendations. Losing the base resource can affect immunization schedule decision support, reminder/recall, contraindication handling, and auditability of historical forecast snapshots.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove or relocate immunization forecasting from the R6 core resource set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `ImmunizationRecommendation` in base R6 as a deprecated or legacy resource while documenting preferred newer workflow patterns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely goal of retiring a dedicated immunization-forecast resource may be reasonable, but the local evidence does not show why that required removing the base resource identity outright. Because every R4 instance and resource-type dispatch path breaks when the resource disappears, a deprecated-retention path would have reduced breakage while still steering new implementations away from the old model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base R6 design would keep `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a deprecated, trial-use, or legacy resource with clear notes that new implementations should prefer the selected R6 workflow pattern. This is not merely migration guidance: it is a base package design that would let existing `resourceType: "ImmunizationRecommendation"` instances continue to validate. The cost is continued maintenance of a resource the work group may no longer endorse and a risk that implementations keep exchanging the legacy representation indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve nearly all R4 wire instances and generated APIs, but would keep an obsolete resource surface and could prolong dual forecast representations.

evidence.detail: R4 contains a concrete resource StructureDefinition for ImmunizationRecommendation.
The assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is absent.
The R6 package index had no ImmunizationRecommendation entry; related hits included Immunization, GuidanceResponse, PlanDefinition, RequestOrchestration, and ClinicalUseDefinition only.
R6 fhir-types includes Immunization but not ImmunizationRecommendation.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a minimal illustrative R4 instance showing the required patient/date/recommendation/forecastStatus shape. In R6 core, the failure occurs at the resource identity before child-element validation because the resource type is not defined.

findings.narrativeMd: `ImmunizationRecommendation` itself is no longer present in the checked R6 package. This is stronger than a normal element change: systems cannot preserve the same resource identity, generated class, REST endpoint, or type-code dispatch. Any migration must first decide what R6 artifact, profile, extension, or archival boundary will carry the forecast.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance can become R6-invalid solely because its `resourceType` is unknown/unsupported in R6 core. Strict R6 validators should reject it as an unknown resource type, and generated parsers commonly fail before checking child elements. There is no direct R6 `ImmunizationRecommendation` instance to map back, so direct R6→R4 representability is not applicable for this removed artifact.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all persisted and exchanged R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` resources. Decide whether to retain them as R4 payloads, map them to an implementation-guide-defined R6 profile, or preserve them in extensions/attachments with provenance. Test parser dispatch, REST routing, Bundle entries, references from other resources, and search/export jobs that assume the resource type exists.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: From a compatibility standpoint, retaining the resource as deprecated would have avoided the hard break while allowing R6 guidance to prefer newer patterns. Removal may be standards-cleaner if the resource was withdrawn, but it forces every existing implementation to handle an identity-level migration.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The absence finding is high confidence. The appropriate replacement, if any, needs work-group or IG confirmation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 defines `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a concrete resource for patient-specific vaccine forecasting, while the checked R6 package has no same resource definition, type code, or index entry. That makes existing R4 payloads with this resource type fail base R6 validation and removes the normal generated class, REST type, parser dispatch, and search surface. Although the R4 artifact is only FMM 1/trial-use, the domain is clinical/public-health forecasting and a current HL7 ImmDS guide still profiles and returns ImmunizationRecommendation forecast results, so this is not merely speculative low-maturity churn.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-ImmunizationRecommendation.json: id/type ImmunizationRecommendation, kind resource, abstract false, FMM 1 and trial-use.
R6 package: StructureDefinition-ImmunizationRecommendation.json is absent; .index.json has no ImmunizationRecommendation entry.
R6 CodeSystem-fhir-types contains Immunization but not ImmunizationRecommendation.

HL7 ImmDS IG source profiles ImmDSImmunizationRecommendation with Parent ImmunizationRecommendation and defines an ImmDS forecast operation output parameter of type ImmunizationRecommendation: https://github.com/HL7/ImmunizationFHIRDS/blob/ee63a21fc92412ed435ce49508d55fe17d4fa39c/input/fsh/ImmDSPatient.fsh
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use substantially lowers the baseline stability expectation, so the mere fact of removal would not be enough by itself. The top-level resource identity break, clinical/public-health role, and ImmDS implementation-guide evidence raise the concern back to Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance whose resourceType is ImmunizationRecommendation has no R6 core StructureDefinition/type to validate against; runtime/API/codegen surfaces also disappear.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base R6 design exists: keep ImmunizationRecommendation as a deprecated or legacy trial-use resource while documenting any preferred R6 workflow pattern. This would preserve most R4 wire instances and generated APIs, with real tradeoffs of continued maintenance, possible dual representations, and slower migration away from a model the work group may no longer want.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Critical impact and Yes less-breaking-alternative judgment, with the caveat that low FMM tempers prevalence assumptions but does not remove the public-health interoperability concern.

findings.title: The local R4 forecasting content model has no same-resource R6 element set

oldState.summary: R4 required patient, date, and at least one recommendation; each recommendation required forecastStatus and either vaccineCode or targetDisease by invariant imr-1.

constraints.human: One of vaccineCode or targetDisease SHALL be present

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 resource had a distinct forecast model: `patient` and `date` at the root, one or more `recommendation` entries, vaccine/disease selectors, contraindicated vaccines, modifier `forecastStatus`, reasons, date criteria, dose/series fields, and supporting references.

newState.summary: No R6 ImmunizationRecommendation resource or same-path elements exist in core.
newState.narrativeMd: Because the R6 artifact is absent, all local child paths are removed as FHIR core paths. Some words recur in R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied`, but those elements describe a protocol followed for an administered dose, not a standalone future recommendation snapshot.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The comparison is path-based within the assigned resource. No R6 resource exists under the same identity, so the R4 local paths have no direct counterpart. R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` has some similar names, but its parent semantics and cardinalities do not match the R4 recommendation backbone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The resource removal makes every local element invalid in R6 core. Runtime code that reads `recommendation.forecastStatus`, relies on the modifier flag, evaluates `imr-1`, or displays `dateCriterion` values has no same-path R6 API. The R6→R4 risk is only informational for this finding because there is no direct R6 element set under the removed resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `forecastStatus` distinguishes due, overdue, immune, contraindicated, and complete semantics; losing or mis-mapping it can alter clinical reminder behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a specialized forecast resource with other workflow or immunization-event structures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 recommendation backbone in a deprecated resource and optionally add links or mappings to newer R6 workflow resources.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing the resource necessarily removes the child forecast model, including mandatory `forecastStatus` and date-criterion content. The local inputs do not explain why that content model had to disappear from base R6 without a transitional same-resource host. However, keeping the full backbone while also introducing replacement workflow patterns has material interoperability cost, so the less-breaking path is only partial rather than cleanly equivalent.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could retain the R4 backbone under a deprecated `ImmunizationRecommendation` resource and add optional references or mapping guidance to `CarePlan`, `ServiceRequest`, `MedicationRequest`, `RequestOrchestration`, or related patterns. That would preserve existing data and generated accessors, but it would also leave two ways to represent forecast facts. Implementers might continue to populate the legacy backbone, and systems would need rules for reconciling legacy forecast status/date criteria with newer workflow representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old child paths, but leaves overlapping forecast models and does not by itself create one clean R6 workflow representation.

evidence.detail: R4 recommendation backbone is mandatory and repeatable and carries invariant imr-1.
evidence.quote: min=1; max=*; imr-1 vaccineCode.exists() or targetDisease.exists()

evidence.detail: R4 forecastStatus is mandatory, summary, and marked as a modifier.

evidence.locator: filesystem path and R6 package index
evidence.detail: No R6 ImmunizationRecommendation StructureDefinition exists to host these paths.
R6 Immunization has protocol and basedOn elements, but they are scoped to an immunization event and do not recreate a point-in-time recommendation resource.
evidence.quote: Immunization.protocolApplied: The protocol (set of recommendations) being followed by the provider who administered the dose.

examples.examplesMd: The same illustrative R4 instance demonstrates the local paths that disappear. A transform cannot simply rename `recommendation` to `Immunization.protocolApplied` because `protocolApplied` belongs under an administered or intended immunization event and lacks forecast status/date-criterion semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: The removed resource carried a compact forecast snapshot: who the recommendation is for, when it was generated, what vaccine/disease it concerns, the patient status relative to the schedule, relevant future dates, and the evidence used. Removing the artifact removes all of those local paths from core R6. This affects validators, FHIRPath rules, generated accessors, UI display logic, and decision-support integrations that use forecast status as a modifier.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For R4→R6, child elements are invalid because their containing resource type is invalid. If a migration maps them into another R6 resource, compatibility depends on a non-core transform and is likely lossy. The most safety-sensitive local validation behavior is loss of the mandatory modifier `forecastStatus` and the `imr-1` rule requiring a vaccine or disease context.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not perform a mechanical element rename. Create a migration decision table for each local path: preserve root identifiers and patient/date metadata, map vaccine/disease context, decide how to encode forecast status and date criteria, and preserve supporting references. Include tests for due, overdue, immune, contraindicated, multiple recommendations, target-disease-only recommendations, and recommendations supported by ImmunizationEvaluation references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible model could have kept the R4 resource and added guidance or optional links to newer workflow resources. If the intent was to consolidate workflow patterns, a computable R6 profile and cross-version extension set would have reduced ambiguity while still allowing the old paths to validate.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the possible replacement is not computably identified, review by immunization workflow/domain experts is needed before choosing a production mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The removed `recommendation` backbone is the central forecast payload, not an incidental child element. In R4 it is mandatory and repeatable, requires either vaccineCode or targetDisease, and contains mandatory modifier `forecastStatus`, forecast reasons, date criteria, dose/series details, and supporting-evidence references. R6 Immunization has adjacent concepts such as `basedOn` and `protocolApplied`, but those describe an immunization event or references to plans/orders rather than a standalone point-in-time forecast snapshot. Existing forecast integrations would need a policy-bearing transform, not a mechanical path rename.
keyEvidence: R4 ImmunizationRecommendation.recommendation: min 1, max *, invariant imr-1 requires vaccineCode or targetDisease.
R4 recommendation.dateCriterion has required code/value children for dates such as due/overdue/earliest/latest administration.
R6 Immunization.basedOn targets CarePlan, MedicationRequest, and ServiceRequest; R6 Immunization.protocolApplied is scoped to the protocol followed for an administered dose.

HL7 ImmDS example populates multiple recommendation entries with forecastStatus and due/overdue/earliest/latest dateCriterion values: https://github.com/HL7/ImmunizationFHIRDS/blob/ee63a21fc92412ed435ce49508d55fe17d4fa39c/input/fsh/examples.fsh
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1 softens the stability claim, but this path is mandatory, central to the resource's actual forecasting function, and used by public-health decision-support examples. Low maturity does not make the direct loss of forecast status and timing semantics harmless.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing the required recommendation backbone have no R6 base path; runtime/API/codegen accessors and FHIRPath logic for forecastStatus and dateCriterion also disappear.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design would retain the R4 recommendation backbone inside a deprecated ImmunizationRecommendation resource, possibly with new optional links to R6 workflow resources. It would preserve existing data, but it would also leave overlapping forecast representations and require reconciliation rules if R6 wanted forecasts expressed as requests, plans, or guidance responses.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact assessment and mostly agree that the less-breaking alternative is Partial rather than cleanly equivalent, because retaining this backbone is useful but perpetuates a second forecast model.

findings.title: Recommendation-specific terminology bindings and status code system are not present in the checked R6 package

oldState.summary: R4 local elements bind, mostly at example strength, to vaccine-code and recommendation-specific target-disease/status/reason/date-criterion ValueSets.

binding.description: The patient's status with respect to a vaccination protocol.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The listed codes come from the R4 local CodeSystem artifact. They are not necessarily removed from the external terminology.hl7.org universe, but the checked R6 core package does not include the corresponding CodeSystem/ValueSet files or a local forecastStatus binding.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had named terminology hooks for forecast status, forecast reason, recommendation target disease, and date criteria. `vaccine-code` survives in R6, but the recommendation-specific artifacts checked here do not.

newState.summary: No R6 ImmunizationRecommendation binding exists; files for ValueSet-immunization-recommendation-target-disease/status/reason/date-criterion and CodeSystem-immunization-recommendation-status were absent. R6 has a related but different `ValueSet-immunization-target-disease` for immunization events.

binding.description: Related R6 immunization-event target-disease ValueSet, not a direct recommendation binding.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 core still has `ValueSet-vaccine-code` and an immunization-event target-disease ValueSet, but the R4 forecast status/reason/date-criterion bindings have no same-place R6 consumer.

facts.note: The vaccine-code ValueSet survives and is not itself the main break.
Related name and expanded concept list, but event-oriented description and not bound by a replacement ImmunizationRecommendation element.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The terminology artifacts were matched by filenames, canonical URLs, and binding names. The R6 target-disease ValueSet is only a possible semantic neighbor; it is not evidence of a direct replacement for recommendation target disease.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The bindings in R4 are example-strength, so terminology changes alone would not normally make arbitrary instances invalid under base validation. However, systems that generated enums, cached package ValueSets, validated more strictly than base FHIR, or used forecast-status codes for business logic can break. If R6 replacement profiles use different event-oriented target-disease/status semantics, round-tripping back to the R4 forecast-status vocabulary may require manual mapping.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Forecast status codes such as `overdue`, `immune`, and `contraindicated` can drive patient reminders or clinical alerts; incorrect mapping can change behavior even if base terminology binding strength was only example.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove terminology artifacts that existed only to support the removed recommendation resource, while keeping more general immunization terminology.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Continue publishing the recommendation-specific ValueSets/CodeSystem as retired or deprecated terminology, optionally with official mappings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: If the dedicated recommendation resource is removed, dropping its recommendation-specific terminology from the R6 core package is internally consistent, especially because the R4 bindings were example strength rather than hard base validation constraints. A compatibility-oriented terminology publication path would still be useful, but it is incomplete and carries lifecycle/maintenance ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking option would be to keep the R4 recommendation status/reason/date-criterion terminology artifacts available in R6 as deprecated or retired artifacts, ideally with official ConceptMaps where replacement statuses exist. That would reduce enum, terminology-service, and migration breakage, but it would not make old `forecastStatus` elements valid in base R6 unless the resource or another base element also survived. Plain ConceptMaps or external terminology guidance are mitigations, not a full backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This helps terminology resolution and migration, but does not restore a base R6 binding path and may imply ongoing support for a discontinued forecast model.

evidence.detail: R4 forecastStatus binds to the immunization-recommendation-status ValueSet at example strength.
The R4 status CodeSystem defines due, overdue, immune, contraindicated, and complete.
R6 package checks found vaccine-code present, but recommendation target-disease/status/reason/date-criterion ValueSets and the recommendation-status CodeSystem absent.
R6 has a related immunization target-disease ValueSet for the disease a dose is administered against, not a recommendation-specific binding.

examples.examplesMd: This fragment is not a standalone resource. It illustrates a forecast-status coding that is meaningful in R4 but has no same-path R6 binding in core.

findings.narrativeMd: The removal also strands recommendation-specific terminology. While example-strength bindings are not hard constraints in base FHIR, many immunization systems use the named forecast status codes directly for reminders, contraindication handling, or UI labels. The checked R6 package does not provide an obvious same-named ValueSet/CodeSystem set to preserve that behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R4 validators would not reject non-member codes for these example bindings, so the independent hard validation impact is potential rather than guaranteed. The practical risk is in terminology service package resolution, generated enums, decision-support code, and cross-version transforms that expect the R4 ValueSet URLs and status code meanings to remain available.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve original codings during migration. If mapping to R6 event/request statuses, create an explicit local ConceptMap and review each status (`due`, `overdue`, `immune`, `contraindicated`, `complete`) for clinical equivalence. Do not assume R6 `Immunization.status` or event-oriented target-disease codes are equivalent to forecast status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less-breaking approach would be to keep the terminology artifacts or publish mappings even if the resource was removed. That would allow systems to validate and translate historical forecast data without carrying the full resource in active R6 workflows.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology server backed by external terminology.hl7.org may still expose some artifacts not packaged here; this report only verifies the local core package contents.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The terminology-specific change is real but weaker than the resource and backbone removals. R4 bound `forecastStatus` only at example strength to recommendation-specific status terminology, so the binding itself was not a base conformance gate for arbitrary CodeableConcept values. Removing the resource-specific ValueSet/CodeSystem files from the R6 core package can still break enum generation, terminology-service caches, or stricter profile pipelines, but if the base resource is no longer present it is internally consistent for R6 core not to carry all of that support terminology.
keyEvidence: R4 forecastStatus binding strength is example, valueSet http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/immunization-recommendation-status.
R4 CodeSystem-immunization-recommendation-status defines due, overdue, immune, contraindicated, and complete.
R6 package retains related event-oriented immunization terminology such as ValueSet-immunization-target-disease and ValueSet-immunization-status.
HL7 ImmDS defines profile-specific ForecastStatus terminology, showing implementers may already specialize these status codes outside the R4 core example binding.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1 plus example binding strength significantly softens this finding. There is migration and tooling friction, but not a strong base instance-validity promise for the exact R4 status ValueSet.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated enums, terminology caches, or stricter profile validators that expect the R4 recommendation status artifacts may fail; the binding alone is not an old-valid/new-invalid base instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less disruptive support choice would be to keep the recommendation-specific CodeSystem and ValueSets in R6 as retired/deprecated artifacts, perhaps with ConceptMaps. That would reduce tooling friction, but it would not make `forecastStatus` valid without a surviving base element and would extend maintenance for terminology tied to a removed resource.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative assessment; disagree with any implication that the terminology binding itself is a hard base validation break, because the R4 binding was example-strength.

findings.title: No computable R6 replacement mapping was found; migration to related workflow resources is lossy

affectedLocation.newPath: Immunization / CarePlan / MedicationRequest / ServiceRequest / RequestOrchestration / GuidanceResponse (possible patterns only)

oldState.summary: R4 offered a purpose-built point-in-time recommendation/forecast resource with supporting evidence references.

semanticText.definition: A patient's point-in-time set of recommendations (i.e. forecasting) according to a published schedule with optional supporting justification.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances can represent a forecast independent of an administered immunization event or an order. Multiple recommendation entries can carry future date criteria and evidence.

newState.summary: R6 core has related workflow and immunization-event resources but no identified one-to-one replacement or ConceptMap.

semanticText.comment: R6 Immunization.basedOn can reference a plan, order, or recommendation fulfilled by an immunization; protocolApplied describes the protocol followed for the administered dose.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Immunization` includes `basedOn` references to `CarePlan`, `MedicationRequest`, and `ServiceRequest`, and `protocolApplied` details for an immunization event. Those structures may support parts of a migration but do not preserve the R4 forecast snapshot without profiling/extensions.

facts.newValue: Protocol followed by provider who administered the dose
facts.note: Not equivalent to a standalone future recommendation.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Candidate R6 artifacts were identified by searching the package index and related immunization text. They are considered migration-adjacent rather than a successor because none has the same canonical identity or complete forecast content model.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This finding is about conversion rather than direct R4 validation. If an implementation chooses an R6 workflow representation, a lossless transform is not apparent: forecast status, date criteria, contraindicated vaccine codes, and supporting evidence may need extensions or multiple resources. Conversely, R6 orders/plans/events that only partially encode recommendation intent may not reconstruct an R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` with the same clinical meaning.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lossy mapping of forecast due dates, contraindications, or evidence can change reminder timing and clinical interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent immunization planning through general workflow/request/event resources rather than a dedicated forecast resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No separate base-design alternative is scored for this conversion-only finding; retaining the resource is covered by the artifact-identity finding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is about the absence of a computable replacement mapping and the likelihood of lossy conversions, not an independent R4-to-R6 base element, type, cardinality, or terminology change. The local package evidence is insufficient to decide whether the standards process intentionally omitted a ConceptMap or replacement profile, so the justification of that migration gap cannot be assessed as a base-design break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A cross-version ConceptMap, replacement profile, extension package, or implementation guide would be valuable migration support, but those are mitigations rather than backward-compatible base R6 designs. They do not make an R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` instance valid as base R6. The actual base-design alternative that would preserve R4 instances is to retain the resource identity, which is evaluated under `ImmunizationRecommendation:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:5d1b91`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Official maps, profiles, or extensions would reduce migration variance, but they would not preserve R4 instances as valid base R6 content and can create competing encodings.

evidence.detail: R6 Immunization can refer to a plan, order, or recommendation fulfilled by the immunization, with targets CarePlan, MedicationRequest, and ServiceRequest.
evidence.quote: A plan, order or recommendation fulfilled in whole or in part by this immunization.

evidence.detail: R6 Immunization protocolApplied captures protocol details for a dose administered or intended by the provider.
evidence.quote: The protocol (set of recommendations) being followed by the provider who administered the dose.

evidence.detail: No exact Recommendation resource successor was found; only generic workflow/knowledge resources appeared as related candidates.
No local ConceptMap or official mapping artifact was identified for a lossless R4 ImmunizationRecommendation to R6 transformation.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is illustrative. It can show that an immunization was based on a request and followed a protocol, but it does not encode an R4-style point-in-time forecast with due/overdue/immune/contraindicated status and date criteria.

findings.narrativeMd: The package does not show a simple replacement such as a renamed resource. Instead, implementers must decide how much of the forecast should become a request, plan, guidance response, immunization-event protocol detail, extension, or retained R4 payload. That is a runtime and round-trip risk because different choices can preserve different subsets of the clinical meaning.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an additional base validation error beyond the resource removal. It affects interoperability and round-trip behavior: an R6 representation built from related resources may be valid R6 but still not reconstruct an R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` without out-of-band extensions or business rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit migration profile before transforming data. For each R4 recommendation, decide whether it represents a future order/request, decision-support guidance, a patient reminder, or historical forecast evidence. Preserve original identifiers, forecast generation date, status, date criteria, contraindications, and supporting references, using extensions or retained source payloads where no target element exists. Validate with clinical examples rather than only schema tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A computable map or replacement profile would have been a partial backward-compatible alternative even if the resource was removed. Without it, independent implementers are likely to create incompatible mappings.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 candidate-resource list is not exhaustive for implementation guides. It is enough to conclude that the core package lacks a direct replacement, not enough to prescribe a universal migration target.

freshReview.narrativeMd: No computable R6 successor or local cross-version map was found for the full R4 forecast resource. The plausible R6 destinations split the meaning across event, request, plan, orchestration, or guidance concepts, and none obviously preserves the same point-in-time forecast status, due/overdue date criteria, contraindicated vaccine options, and supporting evidence in one base representation. That makes migration expert- and policy-dependent, with clinically relevant round-trip loss risk.
keyEvidence: Local R6 package search found no ImmunizationRecommendation StructureDefinition and no exact replacement named Recommendation.
Local R6 ConceptMap/StructureMap search found no ImmunizationRecommendation conversion artifact.
R6 Immunization.basedOn can reference CarePlan, MedicationRequest, and ServiceRequest, while protocolApplied describes protocol details for an immunization event.
R4 resource definition is a point-in-time set of recommendations/forecasting with optional supporting justification.
HL7 ImmDS forecast operation defines ImmunizationRecommendation as the produced forecast, supporting implementation relevance for a computable migration path.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM reduces the expectation that R6 must preserve every R4 migration path, but public-health forecasting and the absence of a clear replacement map make lossy, inconsistent migrations credible enough to merit renewed attention.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: candidate R6 workflow/event resources do not obviously round-trip to the R4 forecast snapshot; runtime/API migration code must choose how to encode forecastStatus, date criteria, contraindications, and evidence.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: For this conversion-only finding, a ConceptMap or IG would be valuable migration support but is not itself a less-breaking base R6 design because it would not make R4 instances valid as base R6. The base less-breaking option is the resource-retention path covered by the artifact-identity finding; a replacement base profile/resource with explicit mappings would reduce loss but still add maintenance and dual-model costs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High conversion-risk assessment and Not applicable base-alternative framing; I would still mark this Revisit because the missing map/replacement creates clinically meaningful migration variance, not just documentation polish.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No R4 local `ImmunizationRecommendation` differential element carried a fixed value, pattern value, or default value; no independent fixed/pattern/default issue was found beyond resource removal.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were identified for the R4 resource-specific elements.
No local slicing definitions were found in the R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` differential. Resource removal dominates the content-model impact.

R4 choice types such as `doseNumber[x]` and `seriesDoses[x]` were identified, but no R6 counterpart exists for a direct type-domain comparison. Similar R6 `Immunization.protocolApplied` fields use `CodeableConcept`, but those are not equivalent child paths.

R4 reference targets were checked (`patient`→Patient, `authority`→Organization, `supportingImmunization`→Immunization/ImmunizationEvaluation, `supportingPatientInformation`→Resource). No standalone target narrowing/widening finding is emitted because the containing R6 resource is absent; `ImmunizationEvaluation` needs its own report.
The local R4 invariant `imr-1` was identified and discussed as part of the removed content model. No independent changed/strengthened replacement invariant exists in a same-resource R6 artifact.
`recommendation.forecastStatus` was a local modifier in R4 and its removal is covered by the content-model finding. No separate modifier-flag flip can be assessed without a R6 counterpart.
R4 summary flags were identified on root and recommendation elements. Their disappearance is a consequence of resource removal, not a separate summary-flag change within a surviving R6 resource.
No primitive serialization-format change was found. The serialization risk is the removed `resourceType` and generated-model identity, handled under artifact identity.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The general vaccine-code ValueSet is still present in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `ValueSet-vaccine-code` exists in both checked packages and still composes CVX and the Australian Immunisation Register vaccine code system. The binding path is removed with the resource, but the vaccine coding system itself is not the main terminology break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: When preserving vaccine context in an R6 profile or extension, existing CVX-style codings may be reusable. The surrounding recommendation semantics still need a target model.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Immunization has partial protocol/dose-series overlap but is not a direct successor
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a breaking change within `ImmunizationRecommendation`; it is a related R6 modeling surface. `Immunization.protocolApplied` includes series, authority, targetDisease, doseNumber, and seriesDoses for an immunization event.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: These fields may help when a forecast recommendation is tied to an actual or intended immunization event, but they do not carry forecast status, recommendation date, date criteria, contraindicated vaccine codes, or supporting evidence as a standalone forecast.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation.recommendation.supportingImmunization` can reference `ImmunizationEvaluation`, and the checked R6 package also lacks `StructureDefinition-ImmunizationEvaluation.json`. That resource needs a separate removal/migration assessment.

R4 package index contains resource-specific search parameters such as date, identifier, patient, status, support, target-disease, and vaccine-type. They disappear from the R6 related index because the resource is absent, but search parameter compatibility is a separate artifact concern.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: Immunization, CarePlan, MedicationRequest, ServiceRequest, RequestOrchestration, GuidanceResponse
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: These R6 resources are possible migration-adjacent surfaces for recommendations, plans, orders, or guidance, but none is a direct successor. A separate design review should choose and profile one or more targets.

The R4 forecast status CodeSystem and recommendation-specific ValueSets were not found in the checked R6 core package. Terminology owners or an external terminology package may define their lifecycle or mappings.
